svg.title: Two complementary boundary-object prediction methods
svg.desc: Shared original GIS boundaries feed fast native LiDAR screening and deeper multi-view review. Versioned unverified proposals remain separate from explicit user review and export. Conceptual diagram, not measured data.

g.text: Boundary evidence: speed versus depth of review
CONCEPTUAL WORKFLOW · more evidence does not automatically mean validated accuracy
Shared GIS anchor: confirmed property + original two-endpoint edges
NZTM2000 / verified NZVD2016 · original mapped flow relationships · source provenance
A · Batch LiDAR screening
Native points + DEM + building masks
Corridors → return groups → aerial/profile atlas
Vegetation / building / unresolved candidates
Fast triage · no trained fence/wall model
No automatic Google or Street View acquisition
B · Skill-guided multi-view review
Earth top + four distinct close oblique views
Street frontage / corners + native LiDAR profiles
Per-edge components, visibility and field evidence
Higher-evidence interpretation · still unverified
Hidden structures and missing views stay unresolved
Versioned local proposal → inspect in 3D → explicit user review
Separate type / height scores · preserve sources/history · export JSON and edge GeoJSON
Independent labels + measured dimensions are required for accuracy claims.
No hydraulic simulation, fabricated fence geometry, automatic field verification or guaranteed completeness.
